title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync covering onboarding status, access/VPC peering, initial benchmark results and tuning suggestions. Redwood to run longer benchmark and share CSV; customer to provide VPC and KMS contacts; security review follow-up scheduled. Agreement on additional logging for evals and slight model param changes to improve latency/cost tradeoff.
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-hour end-to-end benchmark (seq2seq + chat) and share raw CSV + summary by 2027-11-12
Customer to provide VPC peering CIDR, KMS contact, and staging cluster access scope by 2027-11-12
Schedule security review follow-up with Nexa infra team for week of 2027-11-15 (Priya to coordinate)
Samir to provide recommended batch/quantization settings and expected cost delta by 2027-11-12
action_items: Alex Morgan: send pilot pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison doc - due 2027-11-12
Samir Patel: run alignment and latency benchmark on Dedicated pool, share CSV + notes - due 2027-11-12
Marcus Lee: provide VPC peering CIDR and KMS owner email - due 2027-11-12

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Janelle Cruz (NexaHead of MLOps), Marcus Lee (CTO), Anita Gomez (SRE)

00:00 Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check-in - we have about 45 minutes, agenda is onboarding progress, access/VPC peering, the bench results you saw last week and tuning, and then next steps. sound good?
00:12 Janelle Cruz: yep that works, thanks Alex. we've got a hard stop at 10:45 for me.
00:18 Marcus Lee: same here, yeah.
00:21 Samir Patel: great, i'll jump into the benchmark notes after alex covers the access items.
00:28 Alex Morgan: ok quick status from our side - we finished provisioning the Dedicated pilot pool, but it's still behind the peering step so we can't run the full e2e yet. Priya, anything on the onboarding checklist?
00:40 Priya Rao: onboarding checklist - we have the pilot account created, api keys issued to the test team, docs link sent. waiting on the VPC peering + KMS key access to flip the staging traffic over. We've also flagged the telemetry hook for token-level tracing, redwood-console should show sample traces once peered.
00:58 Anita Gomez: yeah, on our side we started the peering request but there was some confusion on the CIDR ranges. i can re-send the exact ranges after this call.
01:05 Marcus Lee: sorry, i think there was a typo in the first email, i will correct that. also KMS - do you need our HSM info or is a service account enough?
01:12 Samir Patel: good question. for the POC we can use a service account KMS key, ideally customer-managed key in your KMS; we support both. if you need HSM-backed keys for production we can integrate but it adds a bit more setup.
01:28 Janelle Cruz: for now service account is fine - production will require HSM but we're not there. main thing is we need to ensure logs aren't leaving the VPC and audit logs are captured.
01:39 Alex Morgan: totally, we respect that. Redwood Private + Dedicated both support customer KMS and audit logs; creds are never stored outside your region, and console access can be limited to SSO/SAML. we'll include the SOC2 docs in the follow-up.
01:55 Marcus Lee: perfect. can you re-share the SOC2 & iso docs?
02:00 Priya Rao: yes i'll attach the security pack with the notes after this call.
02:05 Janelle Cruz: thanks.

02:12 Samir Patel: ok benchmark section - got your summary from last week, and i ran a short reproducibility test on our Dedicated pool. quick highlights: the initial seq2seq workload you sent averages 230ms per token on our test cluster with k-v cache warm; cold start latency is higher of course. cost per 1k tokens was roughly - i'm rattling numbers - around $0.45 with default batching. i have some tuning notes to lower that.
02:40 Marcus Lee: 230ms seems okay but our SLA target is < 150ms for interactive flows, ideally. is that plausible?
02:48 Samir Patel: yes, plausible. two levers - increase parallelism / Ded pool sizing so you have more GPU concurrency, and enable the aggressive batching profile plus prefix caching. also quantization to int8 gives you a cost win but could add a small quality delta - we can A/B test on your prompt set.
03:05 Anita Gomez: curious about the cache behavior - our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes for patient notes. will that see big wins?
03:13 Samir Patel: yes repeated prefixes are where KV cache helps a lot. on sequences with repeated context we saw token cost drop by ~30% in our internal tests. caveat: cache validity depends on model and prompt stability.
03:28 Janelle Cruz: how hard is the prefix cache to configure? we don't want to mess with app code too much.
03:34 Samir Patel: minimal - usually just a config toggle and a small change to the request headers so the runtime knows what to reuse. we can add examples in the SDK snippets.
03:46 Alex Morgan: Samir, can you also summarize the perf delta from quantization? i know the team asked.
03:51 Samir Patel: sure - int8 quant -> latency up to 15% faster on avg and cost down ~35%, but some hallucination rate changed on worst-case prompts; we'll run the alignment eval against your 120 prompt set to quantify.
04:09 Marcus Lee: the hallucination bit is concerning for clinical notes. we need to see the evals.
04:14 Samir Patel: understood. that's why we'll run both the alignment and safety evals plus the latency bench and provide the raw CSV so you can slice by prompt type.
04:24 Janelle Cruz: good. also, can you include more verbose logging for those runs - token-level traces and route IDs - so we can map latency spikes?
04:33 Priya Rao: yes we'll enable token-level traces for the benchmark. Jeff from your infra team asked about retention - how long do traces live by default?
04:43 Alex Morgan: by default 30 days in the console; we offer extended retention as an add-on if you need 90/365 day retention for audits.
04:52 Marcus Lee: ok we'll start with 30 and revisit.
05:00 Anita Gomez: one more infra question - we plan to use GKE in our staging region. any issues with that and the peering?
05:07 Samir Patel: no, GKE is fine; VPC peering is standard. we just need the CIDR and a few firewall rules we will provide.
05:15 Marcus Lee: i'll get that to you.

05:20 Alex Morgan: quick recap of next steps before we run out of time: Redwood to run 2-hour benchmark on the Dedicated pool once peering done and share CSV + notes. Samir will provide suggested batch and quant profiles. Marcus to provide CIDR + KMS contact. Priya will schedule the security follow-up. any objections?
05:36 Janelle Cruz: no objections. just please label the CSV columns clearly - prompt id, prompt type, token count, latency ms, model variant, quant flag.
05:46 Samir Patel: will do. also we'll include a short README for how to interpret the CSV.
05:51 Marcus Lee: thanks.
05:54 Alex Morgan: ok last thing - pricing. we've spoken about pilot credits but you asked for Dedicated vs Hosted pricing. i'll send the pilot pricing + an example estimate for your projected 10M tokens/month usage.
06:08 Marcus Lee: appreciate that. can you show the math for batching assumptions? we want to understand how you estimate the $/1k tokens.
06:16 Alex Morgan: yes i'll include the calculation and assumptions.
06:20 Janelle Cruz: great. that should be enough for today.
06:25 Priya Rao: i'll follow up with calendar invite for the security review and attach the SOC2/ISO pack.
06:31 Alex Morgan: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the benchmark results; same time next week?
06:36 Janelle Cruz: same time works.
06:38 Marcus Lee: yep.
06:40 Alex Morgan: thanks all, bye.
06:42 End of recording

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hears on some proper nouns (e.g., "NexaHead" instead of "NexaHealth" in a quick utterance), occasional filler words included, speaker labels largely accurate though a couple lines had overlapping speech.
